title: European privacy group challenges Scale AI's contractor monitoring
dek: Five complaints target Outlier's alleged trackers, biometric verification and workers' data-access rights.
evidence: Allegations in regulatory complaints; not adjudicated findings
takeaway: Training-data provenance includes worker privacy, consent, identity checks and data-retention practices—not just annotation quality.

sections.title: Allegations

bullets.detail: Noyb filed five GDPR complaints across Austria, France, Italy and the Netherlands, citing investigations alleging up to 19 trackers on Outlier contractor workflows.
The complaints also question repeat identity verification with face video and ID documents, and handling of worker requests for access to personal data.

sections.title: Interpretation

bullets.detail: These are regulatory allegations, not a completed regulator finding. Contractor-data processing needs a separate factual audit before conclusions.
Inventory third-party analytics SDKs, keyboard/mouse telemetry, identity-provider data, lawful bases, access-request handling and retention for human-feedback pipelines.
